10.64898/2026.03.09.710460.rationale: Ex-vivo cell culture study applying COVID-19 patient serum to cell lines; not a human clinical trial.

10.64898/2026.03.28.714969.rationale: Insufficient data to classify; no design, interventions, outcomes, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.64898/2026.04.07.716934.rationale: Animal study (mice) administering anti-CD3 antibody intranasally to model long-COVID CNS pathology; not a human clinical trial.

10.64898/2026.04.09.717442.rationale: No intervention administered; cross-sectional study comparing platelet-monocyte aggregates in long-COVID patients vs healthy controls.

10.64898/2026.04.27.721205.rationale: No intervention administered; observational study of TCR repertoire dynamics in a long-COVID cohort.

10.64898/2026.05.04.722452.rationale: Preclinical mouse model study of SARS-CoV-2 neurological sequelae; no human participants.

10.64898/2026.05.08.26352776.rationale: No intervention administered; case-control study comparing T cell-monocyte interactions in long-COVID POTS vs recovered controls.

10.64898/2026.05.11.26352906.rationale: RCT administering cognitive training combined with transcranial direct current stimulation to long-COVID patients with persistent cognitive complaints.

10.64898/2026.05.13.724894.rationale: Bioinformatic study with no human participants and no clinical intervention.

10.64898/2026.05.19.26353495.rationale: No intervention administered; observational study of long-COVID participants with no treatment arm.

10.64898/2026.06.02.729575.rationale: Animal study (rats) using SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and cocaine to induce long-COVID-like outcomes; not a human clinical trial.

10.64898/2026.06.04.730206.rationale: No intervention administered; observational comparison of cognitive outcomes between long-COVID and recovered African American adults.

10.64898/2026.06.07.730729.rationale: No intervention administered; observational study examining salivary miRNA expression in long-COVID patients with periodontal disease.

10.69855/jhsah.v1i1.361.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.70267/icbms.2502.322328.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.70267/icbms.2502.84100.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.70382/nijefmr.v10i7.020.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.70670/sra.v3i4.1401.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.70822/jce.vi.94.rationale: Completely off-topic; primary outcome is cassava cracker production capacity, unrelated to long COVID.

10.70962/jhi.20250107.rationale: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir given during acute COVID-19; outcome is long COVID diagnosis (ICD-10 B94.8/U09.9) — evaluates prevention of long COVID in immunodeficient patients.

10.7150/ijms.52664.rationale: Traditional Chinese Medicine herbal formulas administered to discharged COVID-19 patients with residual symptoms during convalescence.

10.7150/ijms.77792.rationale: Observational follow-up of ICU survivors assessing post-discharge outcomes; no intervention administered.

10.7189/jogh.16.04162.rationale: This human study independently evaluates culturally tailored Long COVID educational videos that include prevention information, measuring knowledge change after exposure. It is prevention-focused health education rather than a clinical treatment evaluation.

10.7250/bjrbe.2025-20.664.rationale: No intervention, design, or long-COVID definition provided; likely unrelated to long COVID.

10.7416/ai.2024.2617.rationale: Spa-based respiratory rehabilitation administered to patients with persistent dyspnoea/fatigue ≥3 months post-COVID (WHO definition), measuring subjective and functional improvements.

10.7416/ai.2025.2678.rationale: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction administered to ICU COVID-19 survivors with persistent anxiety, depression, insomnia, or chronic pain 1–2 years post-infection.

10.7717/peerj.18705.rationale: Multiple pharmacological agents (CMP, ICS/LABA, Chinese patent drugs, montelukast) administered to patients with subacute or chronic post-COVID cough (≥3 weeks), measuring cough severity reduction.

10.7717/peerj.20211.rationale: Validation study comparing tele-assessment methods for a sit-to-stand test in post-COVID rehabilitation patients; no treatment is evaluated.

10.7717/peerj.20795.rationale: No intervention administered and no long-COVID definition; observational study of hospitalized acute COVID-19 mortality.

10.7759/cureus.23644.rationale: This retrospective observational study evaluates outcomes of targeted/specific antimicrobial therapy in hospitalized adults with long-COVID pneumonia, reporting survival after treatment.

10.7759/cureus.31009.rationale: Pulmonary rehabilitation program administered to post-discharge COVID-19 patients with persistent dyspnea to improve respiratory function.

10.7759/cureus.31281.rationale: Post-ICU COVID-19 survivors with persistent sequelae received an inpatient multimodal rehabilitation program and were evaluated for functional and respiratory outcomes.

10.7759/cureus.33991.rationale: Prednisone administered to post-COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms and organizing pneumonia on CT post-discharge, evaluating oxygen requirement outcomes.

10.7759/cureus.45161.rationale: Long COVID patients (symptoms 3–29 months post-infection) received stellate ganglion block and were assessed for symptom relief.

10.7759/cureus.51543.rationale: Long COVID patients with chronic epipharyngitis received epipharyngeal abrasive therapy and were assessed for endoscopic severity improvement.

10.7759/cureus.54925.rationale: Patients with hyposmia/dysgeusia persisting ≥30 days post-COVID received a two-phase pharmacological protocol targeting inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.

10.7759/cureus.76148.rationale: Omega-3 supplementation administered to healthcare workers with long COVID symptoms persisting >12 weeks to manage ongoing symptoms.

10.7759/cureus.81530.rationale: Dual stellate ganglion block administered to PASC patients with persistent autonomic and pain symptoms ≥4 weeks post-infection.

10.7759/cureus.87026.rationale: Olfactory training with budesonide nasal irrigations administered to pediatric patients with persistent smell dysfunction ≥8 weeks after COVID-19.

10.7759/cureus.87374.rationale: Inpatient PASC patients with residual symptoms received neurologic music therapy and were evaluated for phonation and respiratory outcomes.

10.7759/cureus.88680.rationale: PASC patients with persistent symptoms received stellate ganglion block and were evaluated for overall symptom change.

10.7883/yoken.jjid.2025.222.rationale: Insufficient data; no design, interventions, or long-COVID definition provided.

10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20687.rationale: This multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluates individualized goal-oriented cognitive rehabilitation in adults with persistent cognitive symptoms more than 3 months after COVID-19 infection (long COVID), reporting sustained functional benefit.

10.1007/s00405-020-06520-8.rationale: This prospective human observational intervention evaluation assessed oral methylprednisolone plus olfactory training versus olfactory training alone for persistent post-COVID-19 dysosmia, with independent olfactory outcomes after 10 weeks.

10.1016/j.acvdsp.2021.10.007.rationale: Prospective multicenter longitudinal case-control evaluation of sulodexide for symptoms of long COVID-19 in patients following COVID-19 infection.

10.1002/jcsm.13753.rationale: This is an independent human randomized trial evaluating acute bosentan versus placebo to prevent post-COVID sarcopenia, an outcome assessed through 12 months after infection.

10.1001/jamaoto.2025.1304.rationale: Placebo-controlled randomized trial evaluates stellate ganglion block for persistent COVID-19-induced parosmia at least 6 months after infection. It is eligible intervention evidence despite finding no benefit over placebo.

10.1016/j.bbi.2026.106892.rationale: This reports independent results of a multicenter randomized controlled trial of intravenous temelimab versus placebo in adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms. It is eligible despite negative efficacy findings.

10.1016/j.arrct.2025.100526.rationale: Independent qualitative evaluation of an 8-week virtual physical rehabilitation intervention in people with established long COVID, reporting participant-experienced health effects.

10.1016/j.brs.2025.04.023.rationale: This completed randomized, blinded, sham-controlled trial evaluated anodal transcranial direct current stimulation combined with olfactory training for persistent COVID-19-related hypo/anosmia lasting at least six months, with measured outcomes through six months after treatment.

10.1007/s11357-024-01324-8.rationale: This human pre/post intervention study evaluated one month of adaptive cognitive task-switching training in adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms, assessing behavioural and EEG outcomes.

10.1016/j.bbih.2024.100736.rationale: Four adults with persistent post-COVID-19 condition received active intermittent theta-burst stimulation variants and sham stimulation, with reported cognitive, quality-of-life, and anxiety outcomes. This is independent human intervention evidence, albeit a very small case series.

10.1016/j.jgr.2025.04.007.rationale: G1899 was randomized during acute COVID-19, within seven days of diagnosis, and long-COVID symptoms were assessed through 12 weeks; this is prevention of long COVID rather than treatment of established long COVID.

10.1016/j.clinsp.2025.100614.rationale: This reports independent results of a prospective controlled study in post-COVID participants with persistent breathlessness and other post-COVID symptoms, evaluating 12 weeks of supervised combined aerobic and resistance training (with nutritional guidance, and whey supplementation in one group).

10.1016/j.nicl.2022.103218.rationale: This reports independent results of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in adults with persistent post-COVID cognitive symptoms, including clinical and neuroimaging outcomes versus sham control.

10.1016/j.lanepe.2026.101744.rationale: Independent human randomized crossover trial evaluating immunoadsorption versus sham for established post-COVID syndrome, with clinical symptom outcomes and safety results.

10.1016/j.jpsychores.2026.112605.rationale: The publication reports outcomes for an intervention group of people with post-COVID symptoms receiving PASC-specific inpatient psychosomatic treatment, alongside a control group.

10.1016/j.nrleng.2022.06.007.rationale: This is an original human evaluation of an 8-week outpatient rehabilitation intervention in people meeting post-COVID-19 syndrome criteria, with pre/post and 6–7 month follow-up assessments and an untreated cognitive-symptom control group.

10.1016/j.nrl.2022.06.008.rationale: This reports outcomes of an 8-week outpatient neurorehabilitation intervention in adults meeting post-COVID-19 syndrome criteria, with pre/post-treatment and follow-up assessments and a non-cognitive-treatment control group.

10.1016/j.rehab.2023.101815.rationale: This completed multicenter RCT evaluates a 4-week home-based aerobic and strengthening exercise program with physiotherapist teleconferencing versus nurse teleconsultation alone in adults with persistent post-COVID respiratory/motor disability after inpatient rehabilitation. It reports independent outcomes, including improved exercise tolerance in the severe-intolerance subgroup.

10.1016/j.rehab.2024.101920.rationale: A completed double-blinded randomized controlled trial evaluated real versus sham inspiratory and expiratory respiratory muscle training added to aerobic exercise in adults with persistent long-term post-COVID-19 symptoms, reporting independent post-intervention outcomes.

10.1016/j.visres.2025.108550.rationale: This reports an independent, one-off within-subject evaluation of commercially available coloured overlays in 29 people with post-COVID-19 syndrome, measuring reading performance and experience with versus without overlays.

10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00244-6.rationale: This completed human RCT evaluated acute nirmatrelvir–ritonavir versus placebo and reported 3-month long-COVID outcomes, finding fewer long-COVID cases in the intervention group.

10.1017/cts.2023.154.rationale: A phase 3 double-blind randomized placebo-controlled human trial evaluated early metformin after SARS-CoV-2 infection and reported a reduced incidence of clinician-diagnosed Long Covid, making it eligible prevention evidence.

10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00242-2.rationale: Randomized human trial evaluating colchicine, famotidine–loratadine, and rivaroxaban versus usual care in participants with established long COVID, with fatigue outcomes measured through 24 weeks.

10.1017/s1355617723007592.rationale: The symposium summary reports preliminary results from a pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating CI Cognitive Therapy for persistent long-COVID brain fog, with improvement in symptoms and daily function.

10.1016/j.medcle.2022.12.019.rationale: Randomized evaluation of pirfenidone versus nintedanib in 30 adults with persistent respiratory symptoms and CT-confirmed pulmonary fibrosis at least 12 weeks after COVID-19, reporting clinical, functional, and radiological outcomes.

10.1038/s41467-022-33825-5.rationale: This reports independent 1-year results from a randomized trial of acute-phase remdesivir versus standard care, assessing subsequent long-COVID symptoms and recovery; it is prevention evidence for long COVID despite finding no detectable benefit.

10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00406-8.rationale: This reports clinical endpoints from randomized nirmatrelvir–ritonavir versus placebo–ritonavir groups in people with PASC/long COVID, including symptom-phenotype outcomes at day 90.

10.1093/ajrccm/aamag162.1100.rationale: Pilot single-blinded randomized controlled trial in patients with Long COVID evaluating a high probiotic fermented-food diet, with reported neuropsychiatric and quality-of-life outcomes.

10.1038/s41467-026-75991-w.rationale: This reports independent results of a multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 16-week evaluation of losartan plus low-dose prednisolone in adults with symptomatic post-COVID syndrome and CMR-defined cardiac inflammation.

10.1051/bioconf/20236505039.rationale: This reports outcomes of comprehensive rehabilitation for post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome in 120 human patients, comparing drug therapy alone with drug therapy plus head micropolarization and translingual neurostimulation.

10.1038/s41598-024-61827-4.rationale: This reports independent results from a four-arm randomized feasibility trial in adults with self-reported Long COVID, delivering pacing interventions versus usual care. Although it focuses on feasibility rather than definitive clinical effectiveness, it is intervention evidence and not merely a protocol.

10.1038/s41598-024-68100-8.rationale: This reports independent outcome results from a randomized, sham-controlled 4-week home electrical-stimulation intervention in people with persistent musculoskeletal PASC symptoms, showing improved ankle dorsiflexion strength.

10.1038/s43856-024-00650-4.rationale: This secondary analysis of a randomized trial evaluates remdesivir given during acute hospitalized COVID-19 against symptoms at 1 and 3 months, i.e. prevention of long COVID/post-acute sequelae rather than treatment of established long COVID.

10.1038/s41598-024-53091-3.rationale: This reports independent long-term outcome evaluations in adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms after a defined 40-session hyperbaric oxygen therapy intervention. It is an active-treatment-arm follow-up without a concurrent long-term sham control, but remains eligible intervention evidence.

10.1093/eurjcn/zvag155.004.rationale: This human randomized study evaluates 16 weeks of tailored physical exercise, added to standard care, for POTS occurring after COVID-19/PCC and reports post-intervention outcomes.

10.1093/cid/ciag335.rationale: Phase 3 quadruple-blinded randomized placebo-controlled trial in outpatient adults with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, evaluating 14 days of metformin to prevent subsequent long-COVID/PASC outcomes at 90–180 days. It reports independent outcome results, including clinician-diagnosed long COVID.

10.1093/ofid/ofac492.965.rationale: This randomized trial evaluated early remdesivir during acute COVID-19 and assessed subsequent long-COVID symptoms and recovery at one year, making it eligible as prevention of long COVID.

10.1101/2025.08.08.25333305.rationale: Independent phase 3 randomized trial administering metformin during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and evaluating subsequent long-COVID-related outcomes through day 180.

10.1093/ofid/ofaf634.rationale: This reports independent longitudinal results from randomized adults with established Long COVID receiving nirmatrelvir/ritonavir versus placebo/ritonavir; it is treatment evidence despite finding no significant benefit.

10.1111/hex.70299.rationale: This reports an independently conducted, non-randomized evaluation of a 9-month digital combined lifestyle intervention, with optional nutritional supplementation, in people with established post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), including intervention and control groups and health/process outcomes.

10.1136/bmj.o1212.rationale: This news article reports independent randomized controlled trial results of ENO Breathe, an online singing, breathing, and wellbeing intervention for patients with long COVID, compared with usual care.

10.1152/japplphysiol.00078.2023.rationale: This peer-reviewed randomized controlled trial independently evaluates supervised high-intensity interval training in people after hospitalization for COVID-19, measuring post-COVID functional status and reporting intervention results.

10.1177/21501319261473073.rationale: This publication reports independent results from an 18-participant randomized pilot trial evaluating transcutaneous cervical vagus nerve stimulation plus standard care versus standard care alone in adults with established Long COVID symptoms.

10.1183/13993003.congress-2022.2629.rationale: This interim controlled observational evaluation assesses a hybrid pulmonary rehabilitation program in people with long COVID and reports functional and quality-of-life outcomes versus usual care.

10.1177/27536351241308176.rationale: This reports independent results of a 12-week tele-mindfulness intervention in previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors, begun 12 weeks after infection, with psychological long-COVID/post-COVID outcomes compared with matched non-participants. It is nonrandomized and confounded by concurrent rehabilitation, but observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.1183/13993003.02930-2021.rationale: This reports independent results from an open-label randomized trial of prednisolone doses in adults with persistent symptomatic and radiological post-COVID diffuse parenchymal lung abnormalities 3–8 weeks after acute COVID-19.

10.1186/s12879-023-08172-5.rationale: A placebo-controlled randomized trial in adult outpatients with acute COVID-19 evaluated fluvoxamine given during infection for prevention of post-COVID syndrome symptoms at 12 weeks, with independent results reported.

10.1183/23120541.01552-2025.rationale: This reports independent results of a randomized trial of two prednisone regimens in adults with symptomatic post-COVID-19 organising pneumonia, a post-acute COVID respiratory sequela, including pulmonary and clinical outcomes.

10.1186/s13063-026-09769-2.rationale: Assessor-blinded three-arm RCT evaluating hospital-based and tele-rehabilitation in adults with established long COVID and chronic fatigue syndrome.

10.1186/s40359-026-05149-2.rationale: This is an exploratory randomized controlled trial evaluating a 10-session manual-guided group psychotherapy in adults with post-COVID-19 condition, with reported efficacy outcomes versus a waiting-list/treatment-as-usual control.

10.1186/s13287-022-02972-3.rationale: This controlled follow-up study evaluates intravenous human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells given to severe acute COVID-19 patients and reports 1-year post-COVID sequelae, including fatigue, versus a control group.

10.12688/f1000research.186744.1.rationale: This publication reports independent results of a randomized, placebo-controlled therapeutic plasma exchange trial in 18 adults with physician-confirmed long COVID, assessing symptom/fatigue outcomes after treatment.

10.14739/2310-1210.2021.6.233891.rationale: This prospective, nonrandomized (patient-choice) controlled study evaluated intravenous ozone therapy added to similar medication in 42 people with long COVID undergoing post-pneumonia rehabilitation, and reported comparative clinical and functional outcomes.

10.12775/jehs.2022.12.03.009.rationale: This reports outcomes from a 48-participant rehabilitation evaluation in people with confirmed post-COVID syndrome, comparing two active rehabilitation protocols and measuring cognitive, depression, and anxiety outcomes.

10.14739/2310-1210.2021.3.229981.rationale: This original comparative clinical study evaluated Thiotriazolin added to basic therapy in 15 adults with post-COVID syndrome versus 15 receiving basic therapy alone, with reported clinical and laboratory outcomes after 30 days.

10.1371/journal.pone.0351407.rationale: This reports independent results from a randomized, sham-controlled human trial of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for established post-COVID syndrome symptoms, including fatigue and cognitive impairment. Negative findings do not affect eligibility.

10.1371/journal.pone.0351553.rationale: This human randomized controlled trial independently evaluates a six-week incentive-spirometer respiratory-training intervention for persistent respiratory Long COVID symptoms, with dyspnea and functional-status outcomes.

10.17650/1726-9784-2021-22-4-68-76.rationale: A 60-participant randomized controlled human trial evaluated 12 weeks of BESTFertil versus no additional treatment in men after COVID-19, reporting improvement in post-COVID asthenic syndrome.

10.1177/20552076261428205.rationale: This reports independent pre/post results from a three-arm, nonrandomized pragmatic evaluation of 12-week online and immersive-virtual-reality multimodal rehabilitation programs in adults with established post-COVID-19 condition (Long COVID), versus passive control.

10.17816/rmmar109250.rationale: This research article evaluates a 14-day, two-group rehabilitation intervention in 330 people with post-COVID syndrome/ongoing post-COVID manifestations and reports comparative functional and symptom outcomes. It is treatment evidence, not prevention evidence.

10.23736/s1973-9087.22.07702-4.rationale: This completed randomized controlled trial evaluated four-week home versus inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation in adults with physical and/or respiratory sequelae after COVID-19, reporting post-intervention functional and quality-of-life outcomes.

10.26442/00403660.2023.08.202349.rationale: This original study evaluated one month of L-ornithine-L-aspartate in 30 young adults with post-COVID syndrome and cognitive symptoms, reporting post-treatment improvements in ammonia, liver enzymes, and cognitive tests.

10.29296/25877305-2024-05-12.rationale: Original human comparative intervention study evaluating Selank added to a neuroprotective regimen for post-COVID asthenia and related symptoms.

10.31089/978-5-6042929-2-1-2021-1-54-58.rationale: Reports a comparison of symptom changes in post-COVID syndrome patients with central nervous system involvement who received ozone therapy versus patients for whom it was contraindicated.

10.29001/2073-8552-2023-655.rationale: This study evaluated inpatient rehabilitation in 64 people with persistent post-COVID symptoms 30–40 days after infection. It randomized participants to a multicomponent rehabilitation program versus the same program plus an oral probiotic, with rehabilitation improvement assessed by change in six-minute walk test performance.

10.21802/artm.2023.2.26.14.rationale: This human comparative study evaluates a two-month physical-therapy rehabilitation program for women with post-COVID-19 syndrome after caesarean section, reporting significantly better quality-of-life outcomes than a comparison rehabilitation group.

10.29081/gsjesh.2024.25.2.7.rationale: This reports an eight-week individualized respiratory/physical rehabilitation intervention with a randomized control and experimental group of 24 people diagnosed with long-lasting COVID, with independently reported functional and spirometry outcomes.

10.31655/2307-3373-2022-1-2-27-34.rationale: This reports independent results of a randomized two-group post-COVID rehabilitation evaluation in 37 adults with persistent weakness and reduced work capacity more than 12 weeks after COVID-19. The intervention group received ImmunoActive alongside exercise and diet, with post-treatment clinical and laboratory outcomes reported.

10.30841/2786-720x.1.2024.300442.rationale: This reports an active post-COVID intervention evaluation in 53 adults with hypertension who had recovered from COVID-19 (3–12 months prior). A blinded allocation compared standard therapy plus L-arginine, L-carnitine, and coenzyme Q10 with standard therapy, assessing psychological, cognitive, symptom, blood-pressure, and heart-rate outcomes. It is treatment/rehabilitation of post-COVID sequelae, not prevention or natural history.

10.26442/00403660.2023.12.202523.rationale: This original article reports a 100-participant randomized comparison in people with functional bowel disorder relapse after COVID-19. The intervention group received Zakofalk for 30 days in addition to prior treatment, evaluating post-COVID gastrointestinal symptoms, asthenia, anxiety, and depression.

10.32000/2072-1757-2022-7-140-145.rationale: Controlled clinical evaluation in 40 people with long-COVID, comparing heated oxygen-helium mixture inhalations with a control group and reporting post-treatment outcomes.

10.32592/ircmj.2023.25.4.2080.rationale: Original human randomized, placebo-controlled evaluation of hydroxychloroquine and clarithromycin for persistent respiratory symptoms after acute COVID-19 recovery.

10.32782/2226-2008-2024-3-6.rationale: This original human comparative study evaluated adding sulodexide to usual hypertension and diabetes therapy in people with persistent post-COVID symptoms more than 4–12 weeks after infection, with symptom outcomes assessed after 3 weeks.

10.32902/2663-0338-2023-1-20-24.rationale: This original study evaluated a 10-day infusion regimen of Xavron, Tivorel, and Xylate in 20 adults with asthenic Long-COVID persisting more than 3 months after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, with pre/post symptom-scale results reported.

10.32782/2522-1795.2023.14.9.rationale: This comparative human study evaluates a two-month physical-therapy rehabilitation program in postpartum women with post-COVID syndrome after cesarean section, reporting significantly better astheno-vegetative outcomes than a comparison group.

10.33590/respiramj/93u1v2yd.rationale: This reports independent results from a single-center randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week virtual rehabilitation maintenance intervention in people with post-COVID condition.

10.32782/2522-1795.2023.17.9.rationale: Randomized controlled evaluation of post-discharge physical therapy in 60 adults hospitalized with COVID-19, initiated during the first 6 weeks after discharge and measuring longer-term functional and quality-of-life outcomes. Participants were not required to have established Long COVID, so this is prevention-oriented post-acute intervention evidence.

10.32782/2522-1795.2024.18.13.rationale: This reports independent results from 75 elderly humans with diagnosed post-COVID syndrome, randomized into rehabilitation groups. A developed multicomponent physical-therapy rehabilitation program was evaluated over three months and produced significantly better sarcopenia-related functional outcomes than general-protocol rehabilitation.

10.3389/fimmu.2025.1698271.rationale: This reports independent outcomes from a single-center prospective case series in adults with established Long COVID who received IMC-2 (valacyclovir plus celecoxib), with or without a 15-day course of Paxlovid, and assessed symptom change after treatment.

10.32782/2522-1795.2024.18.3.4.rationale: This human study randomized 75 elderly participants with diagnosed post-COVID-19 syndrome and sarcopenia to standard versus a developed 3-month rehabilitation program, reporting significantly better post-intervention outcomes for the developed program. It evaluates treatment of established long-COVID symptoms, not prevention.

10.3389/fmed.2021.758405.rationale: This human randomized trial evaluated intravenous methylprednisolone given during acute severe COVID-19 and independently reported 120-day respiratory-function outcomes, providing evidence on prevention/mitigation of postacute pulmonary sequelae.

10.3389/fspor.2026.1797346.rationale: This is an analysis of a randomized exercise-versus-standard-care intervention in people with clinically diagnosed post-COVID condition, reporting post-intervention proteomic results. Biomarker outcomes are intervention evidence, although the small sample and biomarker-focused analysis limit clinical conclusions.

10.3389/fmed.2026.1809451.rationale: Reports independent human clinical results for nebulized mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles versus control in adults with chronic cough persisting after COVID-19, a Long COVID manifestation.

10.3389/fpubh.2025.1688592.rationale: This reports independent qualitative results from 20 adults with established Post-COVID syndrome who received an 11-week multimodal integrative day-clinic intervention; participants reported perceived symptom and well-being changes after treatment.

10.3389/fimmu.2026.1813716.rationale: This human study randomly assigned older adults to inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine schedules and evaluated subsequent long COVID outcomes, constituting primary prevention evidence.

10.3390/biomedicines13092267.rationale: This human study evaluated a six-month neurorehabilitation program in 18 people with persistent cognitive symptoms appearing more than three months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with post-intervention cognitive assessments showing significant improvements. It is treatment evidence for established long COVID symptoms, not prevention evidence.

10.3389/fneur.2024.1419134.rationale: Prospective human study evaluating phosphatidylcholine alone or combined with computer-assisted cognitive training for cognitive deficits in patients with established PACS/PACVS; it reports follow-up outcomes.

10.3390/ijerph20156513.rationale: This study evaluated a supervised 4-week multidisciplinary exercise rehabilitation program in 38 adults with persistent long-COVID asthenia and reported pre/post physical-performance outcomes. It is eligible observational intervention evidence despite lacking an untreated long-COVID control group.

10.3390/healthcare14121630.rationale: This study evaluates six weeks of incentive-spirometer respiratory training versus usual care in adults with persistent respiratory long-COVID symptoms, reporting dyspnea, functional-status, and exercise-capacity outcomes. Prior NRICM101 use is an observational subgroup exposure, not the evaluated intervention.

10.3389/fphys.2023.1219252.rationale: Reports independent pre/post results of an 8-week exercise, nutrition, and psychoeducation program in COVID-19 survivors with persistent sequelae, including participants infected months before intervention.

10.35278/2664-0767.2(54).2024.321582.rationale: This reports an independent randomized comparison in 100 women with infertility and long COVID, evaluating a multi-component therapeutic/preventive complex versus no additional preparation. It measured and found reductions in long-COVID manifestations, so it is eligible treatment evidence despite also assessing ART outcomes.

10.36425/rehab90576.rationale: A 98-patient ambulatory rehabilitation evaluation assessed a 21-day rehabilitation programme, with a non-randomized comparison of 40 patients receiving additional hyperbaric oxygenation versus 58 not receiving it, for persistent post-COVID syndrome manifestations.

10.3390/microorganisms12071443.rationale: Hospitalized adults with acute COVID-19 were randomized to a synbiotic or placebo, with post-acute symptoms assessed at 180 days; this is an intervention evaluation for prevention of long-COVID manifestations.

10.3390/metabo16080594.rationale: This is an independent-results randomized placebo-controlled human trial of Lactobacillus helveticus and Bifidobacterium longum in adults with post-COVID syndrome-associated anxiety/depressive symptoms, assessing symptom outcomes after six weeks. It evaluates treatment of persisting post-COVID symptoms, not acute-disease severity or a biomarker-only association.

10.36106/paripex/8204857.rationale: Original research reporting outcomes of a one-week physiotherapy exercise intervention in recovered post-COVID adults referred for rehabilitation, including fatigue and functional-capacity outcomes.

10.3390/jcm14228193.rationale: A four-arm, single-blind randomized controlled human trial evaluated low-level laser therapy (LLLT), transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), and their combination for persistent erectile dysfunction identified as long COVID following COVID-19.

10.36740/wlek202105110.rationale: An original human study evaluated a month-long rehabilitation intervention (physical exercise plus cognitive stimulation) in post-COVID-19 patients with asthenic symptoms, with a comparator group and reported symptom/disability outcomes. It also frames early rehabilitation as preventing long-term asthenia.

10.37506/brrffb35.rationale: This reports independent results of a 4-week comparative breathing-exercise intervention in 60 post-COVID-19 participants, with post-intervention respiratory and functional outcomes.

10.4103/ipj.ipj_234_23.rationale: This study reports an intervention evaluation in 156 people with depression emerging 3–4 weeks after COVID-19 discharge. Participants were allocated to pharmacotherapy plus CBT versus treatment as usual, with post-intervention depression outcomes reported.

10.4081/ejtm.2022.10698.rationale: This reports independent outcomes of a randomized rehabilitation intervention in adults with Long COVID outcomes, comparing aquatic exercise in mineral versus tap water within multidisciplinary rehabilitation.

10.5114/areh.2022.119900.rationale: This reports independent randomized trial results of active versus placebo photobiomodulation/low-level laser therapy in elderly people with post-COVID-19 syndrome, assessing fatigue and functional capacity.

10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-2-7-16.rationale: Original pilot clinical study in 128 adults with post-COVID syndrome evaluating a 12-week cardiopulmonary physical rehabilitation program, with comparative functional and dyspnea outcomes.

10.56936/18290825-2.v19.2025-82.rationale: This reports independent results of sanatorium rehabilitation for patients with post-COVID syndrome, including a comparison of usual rehabilitation versus additional sage essential-oil aerophytotherapy.

10.5960/dzsm.2023.570.rationale: Randomized crossover evaluation of app-guided respiratory muscle training in patients with persistent post-SARS-CoV-2 shortness of breath, reporting symptom and physiologic outcomes.

10.61919/mjxane13.rationale: This reports independent randomized trial results of a six-week low-histamine dietary intervention in adults with persistent post-COVID cognitive symptoms (brain fog), with clinical outcomes compared against habitual-diet standard care.

10.3897/pharmacia.69.e82596.rationale: This reports independent clinical results in 57 patients with post-COVID syndrome, comparing basic therapy alone (n=20) with basic therapy plus thiotriazoline (n=37) over 30 days. It is an eligible non-randomized observational intervention evaluation of treatment for post-COVID syndrome.

10.64898/2026.08.25.26361319.rationale: Reports independent results from an embedded analysis of a randomized, sham-controlled feasibility trial evaluating Microtesla Magnetic Therapy for cognitive impairment associated with Long COVID.

10.70135/seejph.vi.2132.rationale: This human quasi-experimental study evaluates Jacobson relaxation techniques to treat persistent pain in post-COVID adults aged 60 years or older, reporting a controlled pre/post pain outcome.

10.7759/cureus.52935.rationale: A five-patient case collection evaluates off-label amifampridine for fatigue and related symptoms occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection (post-COVID syndrome), with reported within-patient improvement and a double-blind discontinuation trial in two patients.

10.7326/annals-25-03959.rationale: This reports independent results from a multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial of metformin and fluvoxamine given to adults with established long COVID fatigue, with fatigue and quality-of-life outcomes.

10.7326/annals-25-04883.rationale: Placebo-controlled randomized trial independently reports clinical outcomes of 14-day metformin or UDCA treatment in adults with established PASC/long COVID.

10.5114/reum/172575.rationale: This human post-COVID syndrome study compared 102 patients given L-arginine, L-carnitine, and quercetin plus usual treatment with 40 patients who declined these agents, assessing musculoskeletal and other post-COVID outcomes. It is an eligible observational intervention evaluation.

10.1007/s00403-024-03004-1.rationale: This human case-control study evaluates associations between medications/supplements used during COVID-19 and subsequent post-COVID telogen effluvium, a post-acute sequela. It reports fewer cases among vitamin-D supplement users, constituting observational prevention evidence.

10.1007/s00406-023-01557-2.rationale: This human cross-sectional study independently evaluates COVID-19 vaccination before infection as an intervention associated with reduced occurrence and severity of neuropsychiatric long-COVID/PASC outcomes.

10.1007/s10072-021-05744-8.rationale: This retrospective evaluation of 152 post-infectious SARS-CoV-2 patients assessed whether acute steroid treatment was associated with subsequent cognitive outcomes, a post-COVID sequela. Steroid exposure is an intervention; ICU admission and acute severity are not treated as interventions.

10.1007/s40121-026-01362-z.rationale: This is an observational evaluation of prior metformin and SGLT2 inhibitor use and subsequent post-acute sequelae after SARS-CoV-2 infection in adults with type 2 diabetes; it evaluates prevention of Long COVID/PASC.

10.1016/j.bbi.2022.04.013.rationale: This EHR-based cohort study evaluates prior COVID-19 vaccination as an intervention before SARS-CoV-2 infection and measures subsequent long-COVID features over six months. Observational intervention evaluations are eligible even though the primary composite long-COVID outcome was not reduced.

10.1016/j.gore.2025.101682.rationale: This is an independent-results retrospective chart review evaluating N-acetylcysteine supplementation in symptomatic Long COVID/PASC patients, with symptom and von Willebrand factor outcomes compared against non-NAC controls.

10.1016/j.cmi.2024.01.028.rationale: Nationwide observational evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination before infection and subsequent PASC outcomes; it reports independent comparative results in infected adults.

10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e24096.rationale: This independent observational evaluation compares psoriasis treatment groups and reports long-COVID symptom outcomes; IL-23 inhibitor exposure was associated with fewer persistent symptoms after acute COVID-19.

10.1016/j.ijporl.2024.112076.rationale: Pediatric patients with long COVID and persistent postural-perceptual dizziness received vestibular physical therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, and/or SSRIs, with post-treatment symptom, activity, and DHI-pc outcomes reported.

10.1016/j.intimp.2026.116630.rationale: This is an observational controlled evaluation of 3-month Spleen Aminopeptide supplementation in rheumatic-disease patients with established Long COVID, reporting symptom improvement versus no supplementation.

10.1016/j.jadohealth.2025.01.026.rationale: Evaluates multidisciplinary specialist management of children and young people with post-COVID condition and reports six-month functional outcomes following that management.

10.1016/j.lanepe.2022.100485.rationale: This study evaluates post-acute rehabilitation care pathways after COVID-19 hospitalization and longitudinal physical-function outcomes; observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.1016/j.puhe.2024.02.031.rationale: This large administrative-record cohort independently evaluated pre-infection vaccination and acute COVID-19 treatments (favipiravir and sotrovimab) for prevention of long COVID, defined as persistent symptoms at least 28 days after infection, with adjusted time-to-event analyses. It is observational rather than randomized, but observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.1016/j.rmed.2026.108914.rationale: This human observational intervention evaluation assesses whether systemic corticosteroids administered during acute COVID-19 affect subsequent Long COVID symptoms measured from 3 months onward.

10.1016/j.xkme.2024.100835.rationale: This letter reports independent observational comparative results evaluating acute remdesivir use for prevention/mitigation of post-acute COVID-19 kidney outcomes through 18 months in hospitalized adults with reduced eGFR.

10.1016/s1470-2045(23)00056-6.rationale: This retrospective multicentre registry study evaluates prior SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (including two doses or booster) as an intervention to prevent post-COVID-19 condition in adult cancer survivors, with clinical reassessment and adjusted intervention-outcome analyses.

10.1038/s43856-026-01535-4.rationale: This human EHR cohort evaluates acute nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) exposure against subsequent development of PASC/Long COVID, an eligible observational prevention evaluation.

10.1038/s43856-026-01761-w.rationale: This original retrospective observational evaluation assesses pre-infection COVID-19 vaccination and subsequent incidence of long COVID/post-COVID conditions among adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19.

10.1038/s44220-026-00675-9.rationale: This EHR-based pediatric cohort evaluates SSRI/SNRI exposure around acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent incident long-COVID outcomes; it is eligible observational prevention evidence.

10.1053/j.jvca.2021.08.036.rationale: Nonrandomized observational evaluation of acute ICU low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) exposure and six-month post-COVID quality-of-life outcomes in COVID-19 survivors; it evaluates prevention of longer-term sequelae.

10.1093/ajrccm/aamag162.1089.rationale: This matched retrospective human cohort independently evaluates COVID-19 vaccination and subsequent long COVID incidence, making it eligible observational prevention evidence.

10.1093/ajrccm/aamag162.384.rationale: Retrospective observational intervention evaluation in patients with respiratory long COVID; it reports clinical responses after asthma biologic therapy.

10.1093/ajrccm/aamag162.4236.rationale: This non-randomized observational evaluation compares a multidisciplinary telehealth care program for people with long COVID against non-participation and reports 1-year mortality outcomes.

10.1093/eurpub/ckae144.1317.rationale: This survey evaluates use and self-reported effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative therapies among people with persistent post-COVID-19 condition, including those with chronic fatigue syndrome.

10.1093/qjmed/hcab297.rationale: This original prospective study evaluates acute remdesivir treatment as an observational intervention exposure and reports its association with reduced subsequent long-COVID syndrome at follow-up.

10.1097/hcr.0000000000000862.rationale: This retrospective study evaluates an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program in people with Long COVID and reports post-program dyspnea outcomes. Observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.1097/md.0000000000036818.rationale: This human cross-sectional survey compares menstrual outcomes among long COVID patients who did versus did not receive acupuncture, an observational intervention evaluation.

10.1101/2025.03.04.25323101.rationale: The study reports outcomes after IVIG in eight people with Long COVID neuropathy; although uncontrolled and selected for approved underlying indications, it is eligible observational intervention evidence.

10.1136/ard-2022-223439.rationale: This prospective human cohort evaluates pre-infection SARS-CoV-2 vaccination as an intervention exposure and reports subsequent PASC outcomes in adults with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases.

10.1186/s12967-026-07902-y.rationale: This human four-year follow-up compares prior umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cell infusions versus placebo/conventional therapy after severe acute COVID-19 and reports a lower incidence of chronic fatigue-like post-COVID syndrome. It is eligible observational intervention evidence for prevention of a long-COVID subtype, despite treatment occurring during acute COVID-19 rather than after established long COVID.

10.1186/s12982-025-01051-1.rationale: This human case-control study evaluates COVID-19 vaccination status as an intervention associated with reduced need for physical rehabilitation due to post-COVID sequelae, constituting observational prevention evidence for long-COVID-related functional impairment.

10.1186/s43168-026-00587-3.rationale: Prospective controlled cohort evaluation of a bundled multidisciplinary management pathway versus usual care in hospitalized adults with persistent post-COVID syndrome, reporting clinical outcomes.

10.12688/wellcomeopenres.18277.1.rationale: This human observational intervention evaluation compares inpatient dexamethasone exposure during acute COVID-19 with no dexamethasone and assesses persistent symptoms 8 months later; it is evidence for prevention of Long COVID, not treatment of established Long COVID.

10.1371/journal.pgph.0001917.rationale: This population-level observational analysis evaluates COVID-19 vaccination uptake in relation to subsequent long COVID prevalence across U.S. states and globally, reporting lower prevalence with greater vaccination uptake.

10.1371/journal.pone.0296707.rationale: This is an observational evaluation of an 8-week pulmonary rehabilitation intervention in adults with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome, comparing participants who had versus had not undergone rehabilitation and reporting functional outcomes.

10.1371/journal.pone.0312530.rationale: This human claims-based observational intervention evaluation compares prescribed NSAID exposure during acute COVID-19 with subsequent diagnosed long COVID, making it eligible as prevention evidence.

10.14218/fim.2026.00001.rationale: This original, propensity-score-matched cohort study evaluates a seven-day TCM syndrome differentiation-based herbal treatment added to symptomatic Western medicine and lifestyle intervention in adults meeting WHO long COVID criteria, versus the same non-TCM care. It reports comparative clinical outcomes.

10.15829/1560-4071-2022-4827.rationale: This study reports treatment and follow-up outcomes in 18 patients with post-COVID-19 myocarditis; all received methylprednisolone and 10 had outcomes monitored for at least 3 months.

10.17615/2505-jz08.rationale: This dissertation reports an observational causal target-trial emulation evaluating acute nirmatrelvir-ritonavir use and subsequent long COVID onset in symptomatic adult participants; observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.20996/1819-6446-2026-3273.rationale: This original prospective observational study of 129 hospitalized adults evaluated acute-COVID targeted drug exposure (levilimab, olokizumab, or baricitinib) against subsequent WHO-defined post-COVID syndrome over six months. It reports an adjusted protective association, so it is eligible prevention evidence despite being non-randomized.

10.21203/rs.3.rs-440909/v1.rationale: This retrospective observational cohort independently evaluates Autonomic Conditioning Therapy, a supervised physical-therapy rehabilitation program, in people diagnosed with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome and reports fatigue and global-impression outcomes versus non-participants.

10.21926/obm.transplant.2303193.rationale: Reports outcomes after bilateral lung transplantation, including two patients with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis, a post-acute COVID condition.

10.2196/91829.rationale: This is an exploratory observational evaluation of self-selected structured activity-pacing strategies and symptom outcomes in adults with post-COVID-19 fatigue, a Long COVID manifestation.

10.2807/1560-7917.es.2026.31.15.2500672.rationale: Observational claims-data evaluation of seasonal SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in adults without pre-existing long COVID; incident long COVID diagnosis was a specified follow-up outcome and was lower among vaccinated individuals.

10.29011/2688-996x.001043.rationale: This research article reports a retrospective/routine-data comparison in post-COVID patients with long-COVID symptoms undergoing cardiac rehabilitation, evaluating oral L-arginine plus liposomal vitamin C versus standard treatment and reporting functional and quality-of-life outcomes. It is eligible observational intervention evidence.

10.31363/2313-7053-2025-4-2-1202.rationale: This original research retrospectively evaluates associations between psychotropic treatments and post-COVID anhedonia in psychiatric inpatients. Although explicitly non-interventional, observational intervention evaluations are eligible; it reports antidepressant-associated reduction in risk of clinically significant physical anhedonia.

10.33273/2663-9726-2021-55-2-17-29.rationale: This original research reports a dietary rehabilitation intervention in 64 adults with post-COVID syndrome; 42 implemented the dietary program and 22 who could not implement it served as a comparison group, with reported recovery outcomes.

10.3350/cmh.2026.0283.rationale: Observational human intervention evaluation comparing pre-infection ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) prescription use versus non-use and measuring incident long-COVID-related outcomes from 12 weeks after confirmed COVID-19 infection.

10.3389/fmolb.2025.1582967.rationale: This independent-results human study compares people with long COVID receiving prescribed low-dose naltrexone (LDN) with untreated long COVID and healthy controls. It evaluates LDN as treatment for established long COVID, primarily using NK-cell TRPM3 ion-channel function, with participant-reported quality-of-life and disability measures also reported.

10.3389/fmed.2025.1556623.rationale: This human observational study compares QazVac-vaccinated versus unvaccinated people with long COVID and reports clinical symptom outcomes by vaccination status, evaluating vaccination as an intervention associated with less severe post-COVID manifestations.

10.3389/fresc.2025.1633466.rationale: This study evaluates immediate energy-level effects of active, passive, and cognitive rehabilitation therapies in people with post-COVID syndrome. Although its primary purpose is diary development and validation, it reports an eligible observational intervention evaluation.

10.3390/app12084084.rationale: This reports an independent comparative intervention evaluation in people with post-COVID syndrome: rehabilitation plus acetyl-L-carnitine versus the same rehabilitation alone, with symptom and quality-of-life outcomes assessed after treatment.

10.3390/biomedicines14081872.rationale: This is an observational evaluation of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in people with Long COVID-associated major depressive disorder, reporting symptom improvement, response, and remission outcomes. It is eligible treatment evidence despite lacking an untreated control group.

10.3390/covid4090098.rationale: This retrospective, non-randomized matched-cohort evaluation compares long-COVID patients receiving enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) with a non-treated control group and reports symptom and functional outcomes.

10.3390/diagnostics13101755.rationale: The study analyzes post-acute COVID-19 patients with persistent pulmonary interstitial damage who did or did not receive prednisolone-based corticosteroid therapy, with recovery assessed about three months later. It is intervention evidence, though its primary output is a treatment-recommendation model rather than a causal efficacy estimate.

10.3390/jcm12020706.rationale: This prospective international registry evaluated COVID-19 vaccination in hospitalized COVID-19 survivors with underlying heart disease and reported fewer post-COVID symptoms during follow-up among vaccinated patients. Although its post-COVID symptom definition does not fully meet the later WHO long-COVID definition, it is eligible observational prevention evidence.

10.3390/jpm13020182.rationale: This retrospective human study evaluates a two-week multidisciplinary pulmonary rehabilitation program in post-COVID patients, including pre/post rehabilitation functional assessments.

10.3390/life16020319.rationale: This human cross-sectional observational evaluation assesses biguanide/metformin use in previously hospitalized post-COVID patients and its association with lower occurrence of long-COVID arrhythmias, a preventive intervention outcome. It does not establish causality, but observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.3390/medicina61122214.rationale: This is an observational evaluation of self-reported completion of rehabilitation among adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms, comparing quality-of-life and functional outcomes by rehabilitation status. It is treatment evidence, although cross-sectional, heterogeneous, self-reported, and non-causal.

10.3390/v13101904.rationale: The publication reports a human patient with persistent post-COVID symptoms explicitly characterized as Long-COVID who received ceftriaxone and enoxaparin, followed by reported clinical and laboratory improvement.

10.3390/v16060947.rationale: This independent human case-control study compares hospitalized COVID-19 survivors who received acute-phase intravenous remdesivir with matched survivors who did not, and reports post-COVID outcomes approximately 18 months after discharge. It evaluates prevention of Long COVID, not treatment of established Long COVID.

10.33925/1683-3759-2021-26-4-301-307.rationale: This original human observational evaluation compares oral-fluid and hygiene outcomes among patients with diagnosed post-COVID syndrome who used different toothpastes for six months after infection. It evaluates toothpaste use as an intervention for post-COVID-associated oral-fluid changes, although allocation was based on questionnaire-reported existing use rather than randomization.

10.4103/0970-2113.341091.rationale: Includes a retrospective evaluation of multidisciplinary rehabilitation in 48 patients with post-COVID sequelae, reporting improved function and quality of life.

10.4103/tjem.tjem_363_22.rationale: This retrospective observational intervention evaluation studied patients with ongoing symptomatic COVID beyond 4 weeks, comparing JAK inhibitors plus rapidly tapered corticosteroids with corticosteroids alone for postacute hypoxic pulmonary long COVID.

10.48550/arxiv.2310.09446.rationale: This observational evaluation compares post-infection COVID-19 vaccination with no vaccination among symptomatic long COVID patients and assesses CT lung-finding severity. Vaccination occurred after acute infection, so it is eligible as a treatment intervention evaluation rather than prevention.

10.5005/jaypee-journals-11011-0081.rationale: This original single-center cohort evaluates acute VV-ECMO management in adults with severe COVID-19 ARDS and reports post-discharge, three-year functional and PACS-related outcomes. ECMO is evaluated as an acute intervention with potential to mitigate later post-COVID consequences, rather than prior disease severity.

10.51910/ijhdr.v25icf.1580.rationale: This independently reports long-term post-COVID outcomes by prior randomized add-on homeopathy versus placebo exposure, evaluating prevention of post-COVID symptoms and functional limitations.

10.54905/disssi/v26i123/ms157e2161.rationale: This community-based questionnaire study of people after COVID-19 reports use of corticosteroids, saline washing, and olfactory training for persistent olfactory dysfunction and analyzes associations between olfactory training and long-term smell outcomes. It is an eligible observational intervention evaluation, although causal efficacy inference is limited by its cross-sectional, self-reported design.

10.64898/2026.01.06.26343459.rationale: This is an observational evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination administered after established WHO-defined post-COVID-19 condition, assessing subsequent change/deterioration in PCC symptoms.

10.64898/2026.02.20.26346719.rationale: This preprint reports real-world observational evaluation of low-dose naltrexone prescribed for symptom management in 62 pediatric and young-adult patients with long COVID, including treatment continuation, discontinuation reasons, and adverse effects. Although it was not designed to establish efficacy, observational intervention evaluations are eligible.

10.64898/2026.02.27.26347274.rationale: This EHR-based active-comparator new-user observational study evaluates pre-existing IL-6 receptor antagonist prescriptions versus other biologics and subsequent 12-month Long COVID risk in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. It reports independent Long COVID outcomes; the intervention precedes acute infection, so it is prevention evidence rather than Long COVID treatment.

10.64898/2026.07.06.26357398.rationale: This observational EHR cohort evaluates metformin versus DPP4 inhibitors prescribed during acute COVID-19, with subsequent 12-month Long COVID incidence as an outcome; it is eligible prevention evidence rather than treatment of established Long COVID.

10.64898/2026.07.03.26357246.rationale: This human EHR cohort evaluates GLP receptor agonist prescriptions versus SGLT2 inhibitors during acute COVID-19 and measures subsequent 12-month Long COVID incidence. It is eligible intervention-prevention evidence despite finding no statistically significant Long COVID benefit.

10.7189/jogh.16.04164.rationale: Independent longitudinal results evaluate montelukast versus placebo in people with long COVID; outcomes are gut-microbiome measures.

10.64898/2026.07.06.26357401.rationale: This EHR-based observational evaluation compares SSRI prescription during acute COVID-19 with no SSRI prescription and measures subsequent Long COVID-associated symptoms over 12 months.

10.7759/cureus.48591.rationale: This retrospective clinic-based study evaluated inhaled corticosteroid plus long-acting beta-agonist bronchodilator treatment for asthma-like symptoms occurring after COVID-19, and reported symptom improvement at follow-up.
